title: Robustness of mKdV Breathers: A Numerical Perspective
authors: Chandler Haight, Svetlana Roudenko, Diana Son, Kai Yang
abstract: We systematically investigate breather solutions in the modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV) equation via numerical simulations. We show that the breather solutions are stable under a variety of perturbations, including amplitude changes, modifications of internal parameters, and perturbations of the nonlinearity of the equation. Our results are not only consistent with the known analytical studies on the stability of breathers in integrable systems, extending them further, but also provide numerical evidence that such breather-type structures can persist and remain stable over the simulated time scales in some non-integrable settings with symmetric potentials.
summary: This work numerically investigates the stability of breather solutions in the mKdV equation, testing its resilience against various nonlinear perturbations. The authors show that these localized structures remain stable over long timescales, even when the underlying system is non-integrable. The study provides strong numerical evidence for the persistence of coherent structures in complex physical models.
main_problem: The paper systematically investigates the stability and robustness of breather solutions within the modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV) equation under various types of perturbations.
main_result: The numerical simulations demonstrate that mKdV breathers exhibit remarkable stability, persisting even when the system is perturbed into non-integrable regimes. Furthermore, the analysis supports the conjecture that complex interactions resolve into stable coherent structures (solitons and breathers) while shedding radiation.
method: The primary method involves extensive numerical simulations to track the long-term time evolution of solutions, coupled with the development of specific diagnostics to monitor conserved quantities and localized structure decay.
model_or_system: The core model is the mKdV equation ($u_t + u_{xxx} + u^2 u_x = 0$), which is then perturbed by adding nonlinear terms, such as those involving absolute values or other nonlinear functions, creating non-integrable systems.
key_observables: Conserved quantities like Mass ($M[u]$) and Energy ($E[u]$), the $L_\infty$ norm, and the mass of the outgoing radiation are key diagnostics used to track stability and energy dissipation.
important_parameters: Perturbation strength ($\epsilon$), the nonlinearity power ($p$), and the breather defining parameters ($\alpha,  eta$) are crucial parameters varied throughout the study.
main_assumptions: The stability conclusions are based on numerical evidence, and the analysis of interactions in the integrable case assumes that no radiation is generated beyond the numerical resolution used.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of the solution profile, tracking the stabilization of local mass over time, and quantifying the mass and energy associated with the dispersed radiation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first reviewing known analytical solutions (solitons and breathers), then systematically investigating their interactions, followed by detailed studies of specific nonlinear perturbations, and finally analyzing the stability in non-integrable settings.
why_interesting: While focused on classical nonlinear PDEs, the study of stable, localized structures (solitons/breathers) in perturbed systems relates to the concept of robust excitations in complex quantum many-body systems, particularly those exhibiting integrability breaking.
